sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel appearing for appellants that appellants are in jail since 29.08.2023.
They are falsely been implicated in the case.
Earlier, they had lodged an FIR at Crime No.132/2023 against family members of prosecutrix.
Due to previous enmity, appellants have falsely been implicated in the present case.
It is also submitted that there is delay in lodging of FIR.
Prosecutrix is a married woman of 30 years of age.
In these circumstances, the appellants may be granted bail.
4. Learned Government Advocate appearing for State opposed the bail application.
It is submitted that in 164 statement, the prosecutrix has stated that appellants Vijendra and Ramesh were in hand in glove and Vijendra is said to have committed rape on her.
It is informed that appellants also have criminal antecedents.
It is the case of gang rape and offence is serious in nature.
Hence, appellants may not be granted bail.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
6. Incident is said to have occurred on 26.08.2023, whereas report of the same was lodged on 28.08.2023 and statement of prosecutrix under section 164 was recorded on 29.08.2023.
Delay in lodging of FIR has not been explained.
Incident is said to have occurred in a Bara near the house.

Appellant is said to have abused the prosecutrix and thereafter, rape has been committed but none of the family members learnt about the incident when appellants is said to have been abusing the prosecutrix.
Place of incident is also near the main road and other neighbours has also not heard about the incident.
So far as previous criminal records of appellants is concerned, those are not serious in nature.
Except one scratch mark, no other injury was found on body of prosecutrix.
7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I find it to be a fit case for grant of bail.
Hence, this criminal appeal filed by appellant is allowed.

It is directed that on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each by the appellants along with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court concerned, the appellant be released on bail.

8. The appellants shall abide by the following conditions of Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C. as under:-
(a) that such person shall attend in accordance with the conditions of the bond executed under this Chapter;]
Ramesh Patidar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138965755/
2 (b) that such person shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected of the commission of which he is suspected and;
(c) that such person shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
C.C. as per rules.
